days.title: Art 250 Part III · electrodes and the grounding electrode conductor

video.say: 250.50 to 250.53: every electrode, the rod rules

work.q: 3/0 AWG copper service conductors. The GEC runs to the metal water pipe. What size GEC?
work.a: 4 AWG copper. Table 250.66: 2/0 or 3/0 copper.

work.q: 500 kcmil copper service conductors. The GEC runs to building steel. What size GEC?
work.a: 1/0 AWG copper. Table 250.66: over 350 through 600 kcmil.

work.q: 500 kcmil copper service conductors. The GEC runs to a ground rod and nothing else. What size GEC?
work.a: 6 AWG copper. The table says 1/0, but 250.66(A) caps a GEC to a rod, pipe or plate at 6 AWG copper.

work.q: 400 kcmil copper service conductors. The GEC runs to a concrete-encased electrode and nothing else. What size GEC?
work.a: 4 AWG copper. The table says 1/0, but 250.66(B) caps a GEC to a concrete-encased electrode at 4 AWG copper.

work.q: 4/0 AWG aluminum service conductors. The GEC runs to the metal water pipe. What size copper GEC?
work.a: 4 AWG copper. Table 250.66, aluminum column: 4/0 or 250 kcmil.

days.title: Art 250 Parts V–VI · the bonding jumper and the equipment grounding conductor

video.say: 250.102: bonding jumpers, Table 250.102(C)(1)
250.118: what counts as an EGC
250.122 and its table

pages.what: Parts IV to VII: read 250.92, 250.94, 250.104, 250.146, 250.148 from the star list

steps: 250.140 in your 2020 book is the main paragraph and its exception, not an (A). The rest of Parts IV to VII is lookup: highlight it from the star list, do not watch it.

work.q: 2/0 AWG copper service conductors. What size copper main bonding jumper?
work.a: 4 AWG copper. Table 250.102(C)(1): 2/0 or 3/0 copper.

work.q: 600 kcmil copper service conductors. What size copper supply-side bonding jumper?
work.a: 1/0 AWG copper. Table 250.102(C)(1): over 350 through 600 kcmil.

work.q: Three parallel sets of 500 kcmil copper service conductors, and one main bonding jumper for all of them. What size?
work.a: 4/0 AWG copper. 3 × 500 = 1,500 kcmil, over 1,100, so Note 1 applies: 12.5% of 1,500 = 187.5 kcmil. The next size up in Chapter 9 Table 8 is 4/0 (211.6 kcmil).

work.q: A feeder on a 100 A breaker. What size copper equipment grounding conductor?
work.a: 8 AWG copper. Table 250.122, by the rating of the breaker, not the size of the wire.

work.q: A feeder on a 400 A breaker. What size copper equipment grounding conductor?
work.a: 3 AWG copper. Table 250.122.

work.q: A 60 A circuit would normally be 6 AWG copper with a 10 AWG EGC. The circuit conductors are increased to 3 AWG for voltage drop. What size EGC now?
work.a: 6 AWG copper. 250.122(B): the EGC grows in the same proportion. 52,620 ÷ 26,240 = 2.005; 10,380 × 2.005 = 20,815 cmil; 8 AWG is 16,510, too small, so 6 AWG (26,240).

days.title: Theory II · series and parallel circuits

video.say: Unit 14 series circuits
Unit 15 parallel circuits

steps: On paper: resistors in series add; in parallel 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3, and equal resistors in parallel are R ÷ n (three 5 Ω in parallel is 1.66 Ω). Voltage divides across series resistors by their share of the resistance.

video.say: Unit 2 whole: Table 314.16(A), 314.16(B), then 8× straight, 6× angle and U pulls

work.q: A box has four 12 AWG and two 14 AWG insulated conductors that come in and are spliced there, plus two 12 AWG EGCs. No clamps, no device. What volume does the box need?
work.a: 15.25 cu in. Table 314.16(B): 12 AWG = 2.25, 14 AWG = 2.00. Four 12s = 9.00, two 14s = 4.00, and all the EGCs together count once at the largest EGC: 2.25. 9 + 4 + 2.25 = 15.25.

work.q: A single-gang box with internal cable clamps holds one receptacle. Two 12/2 cables with ground come in: four 12 AWG insulated conductors and two 12 AWG EGCs. What volume does the box need?
work.a: 18.00 cu in. Count 8 at 2.25: four conductors, 1 for all the EGCs (314.16(B)(5)), 1 for the clamps (B)(2), 2 for the receptacle yoke (B)(4). 8 × 2.25 = 18.

work.q: A box holds a switch fed with 14 AWG. Two 12 AWG conductors pass straight through without a splice (less than 12 in. of loop). Four 14 AWG conductors come in and terminate. The EGCs are one 12 AWG and one 14 AWG. No clamps. What volume?
work.a: 18.75 cu in. Pass-throughs count 1 each: 2 × 2.25 = 4.50. Four 14s: 4 × 2.00 = 8.00. The EGCs count once at the largest, 12 AWG: 2.25. The switch yoke counts 2 at the largest conductor on the switch, 14 AWG: 4.00. 4.5 + 8 + 2.25 + 4 = 18.75.

work.q: A straight pull through a pull box. The largest raceway is 3 in. trade size. How long must the box be?
work.a: 24 in. at least. 314.28(A)(1): 8 × the largest raceway, 8 × 3 = 24.

work.q: An angle pull. On the wall where the conductors enter, in one row: one 3 in. raceway and two 2 in. raceways. How far must that wall be from the opposite wall? And how far apart must the entries of the 3 in. raceway be, if its conductors leave through the bottom wall?
work.a: 22 in. to the opposite wall: 314.28(A)(2), 6 × the largest (6 × 3 = 18) plus the others in the same row (2 + 2) = 22. The two entries of the 3 in. raceway: 6 × 3 = 18 in. apart at least.

days.title: Dwelling load · the standard method, Table 220.55

video.say: Unit 6: the standard method, load by load

steps: The video starts at 26:25, where the standard method begins. The 26 minutes before it are the optional method, a whole-house calculation, and PSI's journeyperson outline has no calculations section. One line to know from it: 220.82(B), the first 10 kVA at 100% and the rest at 40%.

In your 2020 book the house's 3 VA per square foot is in 220.14(J) and its demand table is Table 220.42; Mike's 2023 book calls them 220.41 and Table 220.45. Table 220.12 in your book is for buildings that are not dwellings.

Your 2020 book leaves garages out of the square footage, along with open porches (220.11). The 2023 Code counts the garage. If Mike adds a garage's square feet, the 2020 exam does not. The electric-vehicle rule he reads near the hour mark, 220.57, is 2023 only: it is not in your book.
PSI's own sample question is a range off Table 220.55. In your 2020 book the oven and cooktop rules are all in Note 4 under that table; Mike's 2023 book splits them into Notes 4, 5 and 6.
One rule this stretch of video does not reach: the neutral for a household range or dryer is 70% of its demand load, 220.61(B)(1). Problem 4 uses it.

work.q: A 2,000 sq ft house. What is the demand load for the general lighting, the two small-appliance circuits and the laundry circuit together?
work.a: 5,625 VA. Lighting 2,000 × 3 VA = 6,000. Two small-appliance circuits = 3,000. Laundry = 1,500. Total 10,500. Table 220.42: the first 3,000 at 100% = 3,000; the other 7,500 at 35% = 2,625. 3,000 + 2,625 = 5,625. (Mike's 2023 book calls these 220.41 and Table 220.45.)

work.q: Table 220.55, Column C. What is the demand load for (a) one 12 kW range, (b) five 12 kW ranges, (c) one 16 kW range?
work.a: (a) 8 kW. (b) 20 kW. (c) 9.6 kW: 16 kW is 4 kW over 12, and Note 1 adds 5% for each kW over 12, so 8 kW × 1.20 = 9.6.

work.q: The whole standard method on one house: 1,500 sq ft, 120/240 V, one 12 kW range, one 5.5 kW dryer, nothing else. What is the service load in amperes?
work.a: 78 A. Lighting 1,500 × 3 = 4,500, plus 3,000 small-appliance, plus 1,500 laundry = 9,000; the first 3,000 at 100% and the other 6,000 at 35% = 5,100 VA. Range 8,000 (Table 220.55). Dryer 5,500 (220.54: 5,000 or the nameplate, whichever is larger). 5,100 + 8,000 + 5,500 = 18,600 VA ÷ 240 V = 77.5 A.

work.q: A 5.5 kW dryer and one 12 kW range. What is the neutral load of each?
work.a: Dryer 3.85 kW, range 5.6 kW. 220.61(B)(1): the neutral for a household range or dryer is 70% of its demand load. Dryer: demand 5.5 kW (220.54) × 0.70 = 3.85. Range: demand 8 kW (Table 220.55, Column C) × 0.70 = 5.6.

days.title: Raceway fill · Chapter 9 and Annex C

video.say: Unit 1, first half: Tables 1, 4, 5 and Annex C

steps: The Chapter 9 notes that decide answers: Note 7, round up only at 0.8 or more; Note 4, a nipple 24 in. or shorter fills to 60%. Wireways are 20% (376.22). Tab Annex C by raceway type (permanent tabs).

work.q: How many 12 AWG THHN conductors fit in trade size ¾ EMT?
work.a: 16. All one size, so go straight to Annex C, Table C.1.

work.q: Three 4 AWG THHN and four 8 AWG THHN in one EMT. What trade size?
work.a: Trade size 1¼. Table 5: 4 THHN = 0.0824 sq in., 8 THHN = 0.0366. 3 × 0.0824 = 0.2472; 4 × 0.0366 = 0.1464; together 0.3936 sq in. Table 4, EMT, 40% column: trade size 1 is 0.346, too small; 1¼ is 0.598.

work.q: How many 6 AWG THHN conductors fit in a 20 in. nipple of trade size 1 RMC?
work.a: 10. A nipple 24 in. or shorter fills to 60% (Chapter 9, Note 4). Table 4, RMC trade size 1, 60% column: 0.532 sq in. Table 5: 6 THHN = 0.0507. 0.532 ÷ 0.0507 = 10.49. Note 7 rounds up only at 0.8 or more, so 10.

work.q: By Tables 4 and 5, not Annex C: how many 10 AWG THHN fit in trade size ½ EMT?
work.a: 5. Table 4, EMT ½, 40% column: 0.122 sq in. Table 5: 10 THHN = 0.0211. 0.122 ÷ 0.0211 = 5.78. Under 0.8, so it stays 5. Annex C says 5 too.

days.title: Wiring methods · Art 300 and the cable and raceway articles (no video)

video.say: Unit 5 whole: circular mils, Table 8, 2KID/CM and the three-phase 1.732

work.q: A 24 A load, 120 V single-phase, 160 ft from the panel on 10 AWG copper. What is the voltage drop, in volts and in percent?
A 40 A load, 208 V three-phase, 200 ft away on 8 AWG copper. Voltage drop in volts and in percent?
A 16 A load, 120 V single-phase, 150 ft away. What size copper keeps the drop to 3%?
What is the resistance of 300 ft of 12 AWG stranded copper?
work.a: 0.594 Ω. Chapter 9, Table 8: 12 AWG stranded, uncoated copper is 1.98 Ω per 1,000 ft. 1.98 × 0.3 = 0.594.

days.title: Conductor sizing · insulation, terminals, ampacity, Art 310

video.say: Unit 3, first half: 110.14(C), 240.4, Table 310.16, correction and adjustment

pages.what: Unit 3 Parts A and B to 3.9

steps: The method every time: size from the 75°C column for the terminals, then check that the corrected and adjusted 90°C ampacity still carries the load. In the 2020 book the insulation table is Table 310.4(A). Highlight Art 310 from its ★ list: 310.10, 310.12 and Table 310.12(A), 310.15(B), (C), (E), Table 310.16.

work.q: A 100 A breaker with terminals rated 75°C, a 100 A load. What is the smallest copper THHN you can land on it?
work.a: 3 AWG. Size by the terminals: Table 310.16, 75°C column, 3 AWG = 100 A. THHN is 90°C wire, but 110.14(C) holds it to the terminal's column.

work.q: What is the ampacity of 8 AWG THHN copper in a 110°F ambient? Three current-carrying conductors.
Six current-carrying 12 AWG THHN copper conductors share one raceway, normal ambient. What is the ampacity of each?
work.a: 24 A. 90°C column: 30 A. Table 310.15(C)(1), 4 to 6 conductors: 80%. 30 × 0.80 = 24.

work.q: Eight current-carrying 10 AWG THHN copper conductors in one raceway at 100°F. What is the ampacity of each?
work.a: 25.48 A. 90°C column: 40 A. Correction for 96–104°F: 0.91. Adjustment for 7 to 9 conductors: 70%. 40 × 0.91 × 0.70 = 25.48.

video.say: Unit 4, the first 52 minutes: the FLC tables 430.248 and 430.250, conductors by 430.22, duty cycle

drill.name: Lookup drill · mixed, say the article first

work.q: A 3 hp, 230 V, single-phase motor. What is its FLC, and the smallest ampacity its branch-circuit conductors may have?
A 10 hp, 208 V, three-phase motor, terminals rated 75°C. What size copper branch-circuit conductors?
work.a: 8 AWG. Table 430.250: 10 hp at 208 V = 30.8 A. 30.8 × 1.25 = 38.5 A. Table 310.16, 75°C: 10 AWG is 35 A, too small; 8 AWG is 50 A.

work.q: A 25 hp, 460 V, three-phase motor, terminals rated 75°C. What size copper branch-circuit conductors?

days.title: Motors · overloads, the breaker, the equipment grounding conductor

video.say: Unit 4, the middle: overloads 430.32, short-circuit and ground-fault protection by Table 430.52, the EGC by 250.122(D)

steps: Overloads go by the nameplate (430.32). The breaker or fuse goes by the table FLC and Table 430.52, and 430.52(C)(1) Exception 1 allows the next size up. The EGC goes by the breaker (Table 250.122).

drill.name: Lookup drill · mixed, say the article first

work.q: A motor's nameplate reads 24 A, service factor 1.15. What is the largest overload setting?
work.a: 30 A. 430.32(A)(1): service factor 1.15 or more, 125% of the nameplate current. 24 × 1.25 = 30. Overloads are the one place the nameplate is used.

work.q: A 10 hp, 208 V, three-phase motor (FLC 30.8 A). What size inverse time breaker?
work.a: 80 A. Table 430.52: inverse time breaker, 250%. 30.8 × 2.5 = 77 A. That is not a standard size, so 430.52(C)(1) Exception 1 allows the next size up in 240.6(A): 80 A.

work.q: The same motor on that 80 A breaker. What size copper equipment grounding conductor?
work.a: 8 AWG. Table 250.122, by the breaker: 80 A is over the 60 A row, so use the 100 A row.

work.q: The same motor on dual-element time-delay fuses instead. What size?
work.a: 60 A. Table 430.52: dual-element fuse, 175%. 30.8 × 1.75 = 53.9 A; next size up, 60 A.

days.title: Motor feeders, air conditioning, transformers · Art 422, 424, 440

video.say: Unit 4, the end: feeders 430.24 and 430.62, air conditioning 440, transformers 450.3

steps: Highlight 422, 424 and 440 from their ★ lists: 422.10, 422.11, 422.16 cords, 422.31 disconnects, 424.3, 440.4(B), 440.14. Six of the seventy are Articles 400–490.

drill.name: Lookup drill · mixed, say the article first

work.q: One feeder supplies three 460 V, three-phase motors: 10 hp, 15 hp and 25 hp. Terminals rated 75°C. What size copper feeder conductors?
work.a: 4 AWG. Table 430.250 at 460 V: 14 A, 21 A, 34 A. 430.24: 125% of the largest plus the others. 34 × 1.25 = 42.5; 42.5 + 21 + 14 = 77.5 A. Table 310.16, 75°C: 6 AWG is 65 A, too small; 4 AWG is 85 A.

work.q: The same three motors, each on its own inverse time breaker. What is the largest feeder breaker?
work.a: 125 A. 430.62(A): the largest branch breaker plus the FLC of the other motors. Largest: 34 × 2.5 = 85, next size up 90 A. 90 + 21 + 14 = 125 A. A feeder may not round up; 125 A happens to be a standard size.

work.q: The standard method, start to finish: a 2,000 sq ft house, 120/240 V, with a 10 kW range, a 5 kW dryer, a 4.5 kW water heater and a 1.2 kW dishwasher. What is the service load in amperes?
work.a: 101 A. Lighting 6,000 + small-appliance 3,000 + laundry 1,500 = 10,500; 3,000 at 100% and 7,500 at 35% = 5,625 VA (Table 220.42). Water heater and dishwasher: only two appliances, so no 75% (220.53 needs four): 5,700. Dryer 5,000 (220.54). Range 8,000 (Table 220.55, Column C). 5,625 + 5,700 + 5,000 + 8,000 = 24,325 VA ÷ 240 V = 101 A.

days.title: Chapter 9, voltage drop and 310 misses
days.what: Your conduit-fill, voltage-drop and ampacity misses, then the four problems written out under them.

work.q: How many 10 AWG THHN conductors fit in trade size 1 EMT?
work.a: 16. Annex C, Table C.1.

work.q: Four 6 AWG THHN and three 10 AWG THHN in one EMT. What trade size?
work.a: Trade size 1. Table 5: 4 × 0.0507 = 0.2028; 3 × 0.0211 = 0.0633; together 0.2661 sq in. Table 4, EMT, 40% column: ¾ is 0.213, too small; 1 is 0.346.

work.q: A 20 A load, 240 V single-phase, 120 ft away on 12 AWG copper. Voltage drop in volts and in percent?
Four current-carrying 8 AWG THHN copper conductors in one raceway at 120°F. What is the ampacity of each?
work.a: 36.08 A. Table 310.16, 90°C column: 55 A. Correction for 114–122°F: 0.82. Adjustment for 4 to 6 conductors: 80%. 55 × 0.82 × 0.80 = 36.08.

days.title: 240, 430, 440 misses
days.what: Your overcurrent, motor and air-conditioning misses, then one whole motor circuit written out under them.

work.q: One motor circuit, end to end: 15 hp, 230 V, three-phase, nameplate 40 A, service factor 1.15, terminals 75°C. Give the conductor, the overload setting, the inverse time breaker and the copper EGC.
work.a: 6 AWG, 50 A, 110 A, 6 AWG. FLC from Table 430.250: 42 A. Conductor: 42 × 1.25 = 52.5 A, so 6 AWG (65 A at 75°C). Overload, from the nameplate: 40 × 1.25 = 50 A. Breaker: 42 × 2.5 = 105 A, next size up 110 A. EGC by the 110 A breaker: over the 100 A row of Table 250.122, so the 200 A row, 6 AWG.

steps: Start by 9 am. 3½ hours on the clock, 2020 code book only, phone face down. No scheduled break; the clock runs if you leave the room.

First pass, done by the 140-minute mark: answer all 70. Any answer you did not check in the book, tap ⚑ under it and keep moving. Past 3 minutes on one question: best guess, tap ⚑, next. Never leave a blank.

Second pass, the last 70 minutes: tap Second pass at the top. It shows only what you marked. Open the book on each one, code lookups first, calculations after. Tap ⚑ again when the book agrees with your answer.
Do not grade while the clock has time and marks are left. Sim #2 was 46 of 70, three short of passing, graded with 45 minutes unused. 16 of its 23 wrong answers were given in under two minutes.
